description: Canonical seed dataset for the Opportunity Index. Field names and value domains match supabase/schema.sql exactly; see docs/DATA_MODEL.md for the contract. Money is integer whole US dollars. Figures are researched estimates for a typical solo operator in a mid-sized US market, not guarantees.

opportunities.name: Digital Product Creator
opportunities.tagline: Sell templates, presets, and toolkits that cost nothing to reproduce
opportunities.summary: You build a digital asset once — a Notion template, a Lightroom preset pack, a spreadsheet model, a set of design files — and sell it repeatedly with no per-unit cost. Margins sit near 100% after platform fees, and the whole operation runs from a laptop. The work is front-loaded: the first product takes weeks, the tenth takes days, and distribution matters more than the product itself.
pros: Near-zero marginal cost — the hundredth sale costs the same as the first
No inventory, shipping, or customer scheduling
Products compound; a back catalogue keeps earning
cons: Discovery is the whole game, and most creators underestimate it
Marketplace fees and algorithm changes are outside your control
Easy to copy — expect imitators within months of any hit

steps.title: Pick a painful, narrow problem
steps.detail: Look for tasks people already solve badly in spreadsheets or by hand. Narrower beats broader for a first product.

steps.title: Build the smallest useful version
steps.detail: One template, not a suite. Ship in under three weeks or the project stalls.

steps.title: Price at value, not effort
steps.detail: A $29 template that saves a freelancer six hours is an easy purchase. A $9 one signals disposable.

steps.title: Publish where buyers already are
steps.detail: Gumroad, Etsy, or a marketplace native to your niche before your own storefront.

steps.title: Build the audience that sells product two
steps.detail: Every buyer should land on an email list. That list is the real asset.

opportunities.name: E-Commerce Store
opportunities.tagline: Own the brand, the margin, and the customer relationship
opportunities.summary: A branded store selling physical products you source, private-label, or make. Unlike dropshipping, you hold inventory — which is exactly why the margins and the defensibility are better. The constraint is cash: every dollar of growth ties up another dollar of stock, and the businesses that fail usually die solvent-on-paper but out of cash.
pros: Real enterprise value — stores with traction sell for 2-4x annual profit
You own the customer list and the repeat purchase
Product margin gives room to buy traffic profitably
cons: Inventory ties up cash and can go stale
Ad costs rise every year; unit economics need constant attention
Returns, chargebacks, and support are a permanent tax on your time

steps.title: Choose a category you can restock reliably
steps.detail: Lead times and MOQs decide your cash cycle more than product choice does.

steps.title: Validate with a small first order
steps.detail: A few hundred units, sold manually, tells you more than any survey.

steps.title: Get unit economics on paper
steps.detail: Landed cost, fees, shipping, returns, and target CAC. If contribution margin is under 40%, fix it before scaling.

steps.title: Launch a narrow catalogue
steps.detail: Three to five SKUs. Depth beats breadth until you know what sells.

steps.title: Buy traffic only once organic converts
steps.detail: Paid ads amplify a working funnel; they do not create one.

opportunities.name: Social Media Manager
opportunities.tagline: Run the accounts small businesses know they are neglecting
opportunities.summary: Local businesses and small brands need consistent posting, community replies, and a monthly report — and most owners will never do it themselves. Retainers run $500-$2,000 per client per month, and three to six clients is a full practice. The work is genuinely repeatable, which is what makes it a good first service business.
pros: Starts at zero cost with tools you already have
Monthly retainers make income predictable
Skills transfer directly into higher-paid marketing work
cons: Crowded field — differentiation has to be niche or results
Clients judge you on metrics you only partly control
Revenue is capped by hours unless you hire

steps.title: Pick one industry
steps.detail: "Social for dental practices" wins the pitch that "social media manager" loses.

steps.title: Build two speculative case studies
steps.detail: Rework a real local business's feed and show the before/after. It replaces a portfolio.

steps.title: Price as a monthly retainer
steps.detail: Scope it precisely: post count, platforms, reporting cadence, revision limits.

steps.title: Systematise production
steps.detail: Batch a month of content in two days; the rest is scheduling and replies.

steps.title: Raise prices at every third client
steps.detail: Demand at your current price is the signal to move up.

opportunities.name: Cleaning Service
opportunities.tagline: Recurring local revenue with almost no technical barrier
opportunities.summary: Residential and small-office cleaning is unglamorous, durable, and one of the fastest paths from zero to real monthly revenue. Recurring bi-weekly contracts mean a client won in month one is still paying in month twenty. The hard part is not cleaning — it is hiring and keeping reliable people once you stop doing the work yourself.
pros: Recurring contracts produce stable, forecastable revenue
Cash-flow positive almost immediately — clients pay per visit
Genuinely sellable: cleaning books trade on established multiples
cons: Labour turnover is the defining operational problem
Physically demanding until you can afford to staff it
Insurance, bonding, and payroll compliance arrive early

steps.title: Choose residential or commercial
steps.detail: Residential starts faster; commercial pays more per contract and runs at night.

steps.title: Get insured and bonded first
steps.detail: Roughly $500-$1,200 a year, and it is the first thing a serious client asks for.

steps.title: Land the first ten clients by hand
steps.detail: Door hangers, neighbourhood groups, and Google Business Profile beat paid ads at this size.

steps.title: Standardise the checklist
steps.detail: A written per-room checklist is what lets someone else do the job to your standard.

steps.title: Hire before you are ready
steps.detail: Your first employee is the difference between a job and a business.

opportunities.name: Website Developer
opportunities.tagline: Project fees now, maintenance retainers forever
opportunities.summary: Small businesses still buy websites, and they buy them from people who answer the phone. Build-outs run $2,000-$10,000; the durable money is in the $150-$500 monthly care plans that follow. AI tooling has compressed build time far more than it has compressed what clients will pay.
pros: High hourly value once you have a repeatable stack
Maintenance plans convert one-off projects into recurring revenue
Every project is a referral source in a tight local market
cons: Scope creep destroys margin on fixed-fee work
Template builders have compressed the low end of the market
Feast-or-famine unless you keep a pipeline while delivering

steps.title: Standardise on one stack
steps.detail: One CMS, one hosting setup, one component kit. Variety is what makes projects unprofitable.

steps.title: Sell outcomes, not pages
steps.detail: "More booked calls" is a budget line; "a 5-page site" is a commodity.

steps.title: Take 50% up front, always
steps.detail: It filters out the clients who were never going to pay.

steps.title: Attach a care plan to every proposal
steps.detail: Hosting, updates, backups, and small edits. Most clients accept it by default.

steps.title: Productise a fixed-price starter
steps.detail: One tier, one timeline, one price — it closes far faster than custom quotes.

opportunities.name: Podcast Producer
opportunities.tagline: Edit, package, and distribute for people who only want to talk
opportunities.summary: Founders, coaches, and agencies start podcasts and abandon them at episode six, because editing is the part nobody enjoys. A producer takes the raw file and returns a finished episode, show notes, and a handful of clips. Retainers run $800-$2,500 per show, and one client typically means four episodes a month.
pros: Retainer work with a predictable weekly rhythm
Clip repurposing lets you upsell without new client acquisition
Software has made the technical bar much lower than clients assume
cons: Shows get cancelled — churn is real and unpredictable
Turnaround expectations compress your schedule
Rate pressure from cheap overseas editing services

steps.title: Master one editing workflow
steps.detail: Descript or Premiere end-to-end. Speed comes from repetition, not from tools.

steps.title: Offer a free first episode
steps.detail: The finished episode is the pitch; nobody buys audio editing from a description.

steps.title: Bundle clips and show notes
steps.detail: This is what moves you from $500 to $1,500 a month per client.

steps.title: Cap revisions in the agreement
steps.detail: Two rounds. Unlimited revisions is how producers end up working for minimum wage.

steps.title: Hire an assistant editor at four clients
steps.detail: You review and deliver; they do first-pass cuts.

opportunities.name: Personal Trainer
opportunities.tagline: Certification, a handful of clients, and a strong local reputation
opportunities.summary: Sessions run $60-$120 an hour, and a trainer with fifteen regular clients is running a solid full-time business. Certification and insurance are the entry cost. The ceiling comes from hours in a day — which is why the trainers who earn most run small groups or a hybrid online programme alongside one-to-one work.
pros: Strong hourly rate from the very first client
Clients stay for years when results are real
Small-group and online tiers break the hourly ceiling
cons: Early mornings and evenings are when clients want you
Income stops the moment you do — no passive component by default
Certification, insurance, and gym rent before any revenue

steps.title: Get an accredited certification
steps.detail: NASM, ACE, or ISSA. Roughly $700-$2,000 including the exam.

steps.title: Secure liability insurance
steps.detail: Non-negotiable, and required before any gym will rent you floor space.

steps.title: Train your first five for free
steps.detail: In exchange for testimonials and before/after photos. It builds the proof you need.

steps.title: Sell packages, not sessions
steps.detail: Ten-session blocks improve cash flow and roughly double client adherence.

steps.title: Add a small-group tier
steps.detail: Four clients at $35 beats one at $90 for the same hour of your time.

opportunities.name: Print on Demand
opportunities.tagline: Design once; a partner prints, packs, and ships each order
opportunities.summary: You upload designs; a fulfilment partner prints on demand and ships direct. There is no inventory and effectively no downside risk, which is exactly why the market is saturated and margins are thin. It works as a low-stakes way to test whether you can sell anything at all, and as a bolt-on for creators who already have an audience.
pros: Lowest startup cost of anything in the index
No inventory risk whatsoever
Pairs naturally with an existing audience
cons: Base costs leave $4-$8 of margin per shirt
Extremely crowded — most stores never make a sale
You control neither print quality nor shipping times

steps.title: Target a niche identity, not a broad joke
steps.detail: "Retired air-traffic controller" outsells "funny cat shirt" every time.

steps.title: Design for the platform's search
steps.detail: On Amazon Merch and Etsy, keyword research matters more than aesthetics.

steps.title: Order samples of your best sellers
steps.detail: You cannot support a product whose quality you have never seen.

steps.title: Publish in volume
steps.detail: A handful of designs is not a test. Fifty is.

steps.title: Move winners onto better margins
steps.detail: Once a design sells consistently, bulk printing doubles the profit per unit.

opportunities.name: Freelance Writing
opportunities.tagline: Words businesses need and do not have time to produce
opportunities.summary: Blog posts, case studies, email sequences, and white papers still get commissioned — but the bottom of the market has been hollowed out by generative tools. What sells now is judgement, interviews, and subject-matter depth. Generalists competing on price are in trouble; a writer who genuinely understands SaaS security or commercial insurance is booked out.
pros: Zero startup cost and an immediate start
Specialists command $0.50-$2.00 a word
Portfolio compounds; good clips keep earning you work
cons: The commodity end of the market has collapsed
Income is strictly per-project unless you retain clients
Chasing invoices is a permanent part of the job

steps.title: Choose a lucrative vertical
steps.detail: Fintech, healthcare, B2B SaaS, and legal pay multiples of lifestyle content.

steps.title: Publish three strong clips
steps.detail: Self-published is fine. Editors care about the writing, not the masthead.

steps.title: Pitch companies, not job boards
steps.detail: Boards are a race to the bottom; a direct pitch to a marketing lead is not.

steps.title: Price per project, never per hour
steps.detail: Getting faster should not cut your pay.

steps.title: Convert clients to monthly retainers
steps.detail: Four posts a month, invoiced on the first. It ends the feast-or-famine cycle.

opportunities.name: Virtual Assistant
opportunities.tagline: Take the admin off a busy operator's plate, remotely
opportunities.summary: Inbox triage, scheduling, data entry, invoicing, travel, light bookkeeping — the work every small operator resents. US-based VAs bill $20-$50 an hour, and the ones who earn at the top of that range have specialised into something specific: podcast admin, real-estate transaction coordination, e-commerce customer service.
pros: Start today with no money and no equipment
Clients rarely leave once you know their systems
A direct window into how many small businesses actually run
cons: Heavy price pressure from offshore providers
Hourly by nature — scaling means becoming an agency
Scope drifts constantly unless you defend it

steps.title: Specialise immediately
steps.detail: "VA for real-estate agents" is a business; "virtual assistant" is a commodity.

steps.title: Learn the niche's stack
steps.detail: Knowing the exact CRM your clients use is worth $15 an hour by itself.

steps.title: Sell retainer blocks
steps.detail: 20 hours a month, invoiced up front. It beats hourly billing on both sides.

steps.title: Document every process
steps.detail: Your SOP library is what lets you hand work to a subcontractor later.

steps.title: Subcontract the routine work
steps.detail: Keep the client relationship; delegate the data entry.

opportunities.name: Affiliate Marketing
opportunities.tagline: Earn commission sending qualified buyers to products you trust
opportunities.summary: You build an audience or a content asset, recommend products, and take a cut of what converts. The economics are excellent and the timeline is brutal: most sites see meaningful revenue somewhere between month nine and month eighteen. Search-algorithm volatility has made single-channel affiliate businesses considerably riskier than they were five years ago.
pros: No product, inventory, support, or fulfilment
Income continues from content published years ago
Scales without adding hours once ranking
cons: Long runway before the first meaningful cheque
One algorithm update can halve revenue overnight
Programmes change commission rates without warning

steps.title: Pick a niche with real purchase intent
steps.detail: People must be searching to buy, not just to read.

steps.title: Choose the channel you will actually sustain
steps.detail: SEO site, YouTube, or a newsletter. One, done properly, for a year.

steps.title: Buy and test what you recommend
steps.detail: First-hand testing is the only durable edge left in affiliate content.

steps.title: Get into higher-paying programmes
steps.detail: Software and financial products pay 20-40%; general retail pays 3%.

steps.title: Capture emails from day one
steps.detail: It is the only channel no platform can take away from you.

opportunities.name: YouTube Channel
opportunities.tagline: Build an audience that ad revenue, sponsors, and products all pay for
opportunities.summary: The highest ceiling and one of the longest runways in the index. Ad revenue alone is modest — $3-$20 per thousand views depending on niche — but a channel with 20,000 engaged subscribers supports sponsorships, an email list, and product sales. Roughly nine in ten channels are abandoned before the algorithm has enough data to distribute them.
pros: Compounding: the back catalogue keeps earning indefinitely
Multiple revenue lines from one audience
Sponsorships pay far more than platform ad revenue
cons: Twelve to eighteen months of work before meaningful income is normal
Production time per video is consistently underestimated
Being the face of the channel is hard to delegate later

steps.title: Choose a niche with commercial sponsors
steps.detail: Finance, software, and home improvement pay many times what entertainment does.

steps.title: Study packaging before production
steps.detail: Title and thumbnail decide whether the video is ever seen. Design them first.

steps.title: Publish weekly for six months
steps.detail: Consistency is the input the algorithm actually rewards.

steps.title: Review retention on every video
steps.detail: The first thirty seconds explain most of your performance.

steps.title: Diversify the moment you monetise
steps.detail: Ad revenue is the floor, not the plan. Sponsors and products are the business.

opportunities.name: Bookkeeping Service
opportunities.tagline: Monthly closes for small businesses that dread their own books
opportunities.summary: Every small business needs its books closed monthly, and almost none of them want to do it. Retainers run $300-$1,500 per client per month and clients stay for years — switching bookkeepers is genuinely painful. It is one of the quietest, stickiest service businesses available, and demand exceeds supply in most markets.
pros: Exceptionally low churn — multi-year client relationships are normal
Recurring revenue from month one
Underserved: many bookkeepers have waiting lists
cons: January to April is relentless
Errors carry real financial consequences for clients
Certification and software costs come before revenue

steps.title: Get QuickBooks or Xero certified
steps.detail: Free through the vendors and it is the credential clients actually recognise.

steps.title: Specialise by industry
steps.detail: Restaurants, trades, and e-commerce each have distinct books. Depth wins referrals.

steps.title: Price by transaction volume
steps.detail: Not by hours — it protects your margin as you get faster.

steps.title: Standardise the monthly close
steps.detail: A fixed checklist and calendar is what makes the practice scalable.

steps.title: Partner with a CPA firm
steps.detail: They want the compliance work, not the bookkeeping. Referrals flow both ways.

opportunities.name: Lawn Care & Landscaping
opportunities.tagline: Weekly routes that pay for themselves inside a season
opportunities.summary: A route of forty weekly lawns at $45 each is roughly $7,200 a month in season. Density is everything: tightly clustered clients cut drive time and double effective hourly rate. In most of the country the business is seasonal, so the operators who do well either add snow removal and leaf clean-up or bank aggressively through summer.
pros: Recurring weekly revenue with very high retention
Equipment is a real, resellable asset
Route density compounds your margin as you grow
cons: Seasonal in most climates
Meaningful equipment investment up front
Weather sets your schedule, not you

steps.title: Buy quality used equipment
steps.detail: A commercial mower at half price beats a new residential one that dies in July.

steps.title: Farm one neighbourhood at a time
steps.detail: Twenty lawns on three streets beats forty spread across a county.

steps.title: Sell the season, not the cut
steps.detail: Contracted monthly billing March-October smooths cash flow.

steps.title: Upsell mulch, aeration, and clean-ups
steps.detail: One-off jobs at high margin between the weekly route.

steps.title: Add a winter service
steps.detail: Snow removal or holiday lighting keeps crew and cash flow through the off-season.

opportunities.name: Mobile Car Detailing
opportunities.tagline: Drive to the customer; charge premium for the convenience
opportunities.summary: Full details run $150-$350 and take three to five hours, with consumables costing under $20 a car. Going mobile removes the rent line entirely and is what customers pay the premium for. Growth comes from fleet and dealership contracts, which trade the higher per-car price for guaranteed weekly volume.
pros: Very high margin per job — consumables are a rounding error
No premises, no rent, no lease
Fleet and dealer contracts provide a stable base
cons: Physically hard work in whatever weather arrives
Water and power access varies by site
Capped by how many cars fit in a day

steps.title: Kit out a van or trailer
steps.detail: Water tank, generator, pressure washer, extractor. Around $3,000-$6,000 done properly.

steps.title: Learn paint correction
steps.detail: It is the difference between a $120 wash and a $400 detail.

steps.title: Photograph every single job
steps.detail: Before/after shots are the entire marketing strategy in this trade.

steps.title: Sell maintenance plans
steps.detail: Monthly upkeep details at a lower price point, booked in advance.

steps.title: Chase fleet contracts
steps.detail: Dealerships, rental branches, and company fleets fill weekdays reliably.

opportunities.name: Newsletter Publisher
opportunities.tagline: An owned audience that sponsors will pay to reach
opportunities.summary: A niche newsletter with 5,000 engaged subscribers can command $300-$800 per sponsored slot, and unlike social platforms, nobody can throttle your distribution. It is one of the few genuinely ownable audience assets. Growth is the hard part — organic list building is slow, and paid acquisition only works if your monetisation is already proven.
pros: You own the distribution outright
Sponsorship rates hold up even at modest list sizes
Very low ongoing cost; margins are near total
cons: Growth from a standing start is genuinely slow
A weekly send is a weekly obligation, indefinitely
Deliverability and inbox placement are constant maintenance

steps.title: Pick a niche advertisers want
steps.detail: B2B and finance sponsors pay far more per subscriber than general interest.

steps.title: Commit to a fixed cadence
steps.detail: Weekly, same day. Irregular sends kill open rates faster than bad writing.

steps.title: Grow through cross-promotion
steps.detail: Swaps with adjacent newsletters are the cheapest quality growth available.

steps.title: Publish a rate card at 2,000 subscribers
steps.detail: Sponsors will not ask; you have to make the offer visible.

steps.title: Add a paid tier once free is working
steps.detail: Premium issues or a community, priced at $8-$20 a month.

opportunities.name: Airbnb Co-Hosting
opportunities.tagline: Run other people's short-term rentals for a share of revenue
opportunities.summary: You handle listings, pricing, guest communication, and cleaning coordination; the owner keeps the property and pays you 15-25% of booking revenue. No mortgage, no down payment, no exposure to the asset. Ten properties at $400 a month each is a real business, and the model works precisely because most owners badly underestimate the operational load.
pros: Access short-term rental income without owning property
Revenue share scales with the market, not a fixed fee
Systems and cleaner networks carry across every new property
cons: Guest issues arrive at 2am and are yours to solve
Regulation on short-term rentals keeps tightening in many cities
Losing one owner can be a large share of revenue

steps.title: Learn one market deeply
steps.detail: Occupancy patterns, seasonality, and local rules for a single city.

steps.title: Co-host one property brilliantly
steps.detail: Your first owner's numbers are the case study that wins the next five.

steps.title: Build the cleaner and handyman bench
steps.detail: Reliable turnovers are the operational core of the whole service.

steps.title: Use dynamic pricing
steps.detail: Automated pricing typically lifts revenue 10-25% over fixed nightly rates.

steps.title: Contract on revenue share
steps.detail: 20% of gross aligns you with the owner far better than a flat fee.

opportunities.name: Online Course Creator
opportunities.tagline: Package what you know into something that sells while you sleep
opportunities.summary: A $300 course sold 40 times a month is $12,000 in revenue with essentially no marginal cost. The catch is that courses do not sell themselves — you need an audience or a paid funnel that works, and the failure mode is spending three months building a course for an audience that does not exist. Sell it first, build it second.
pros: Very high margin and fully scalable
Establishes authority that feeds consulting and speaking
One good course can sell for years with light updates
cons: Requires an audience or a working ad funnel first
Content ages and needs periodic re-recording
Refund rates run 5-15% on cold traffic

steps.title: Pre-sell before you build
steps.detail: Take deposits on an outline. No takers means no course — you just saved three months.

steps.title: Teach one specific transformation
steps.detail: "Land your first three bookkeeping clients" beats "learn bookkeeping".

steps.title: Keep production lean
steps.detail: Screen recording and a decent microphone. Nobody refunds over lighting.

steps.title: Price for outcome, not length
steps.detail: A four-hour course that gets someone hired is worth more than forty hours of theory.

steps.title: Run live cohorts first
steps.detail: Higher price, faster feedback, and the recordings become the evergreen version.

opportunities.name: Pressure Washing
opportunities.tagline: Visible results, immediate payment, low barrier to entry
opportunities.summary: Driveways, siding, and decks at $200-$600 a job, most completed in two to four hours. The before/after contrast is so dramatic that the marketing largely does itself on local social feeds. Commercial work — storefronts, parking structures, restaurant pads — is where the recurring contracts and the better rates live.
pros: Fast jobs and same-day payment
Results photograph extremely well, which drives referrals
Commercial contracts turn one-off work into recurring revenue
cons: Damaging a surface is an expensive, avoidable mistake
Weather-dependent and seasonal in cold climates
Low barrier means constant new local competitors

steps.title: Buy commercial-grade gear
steps.detail: 4 GPM minimum with a surface cleaner. Consumer units cannot do this work.

steps.title: Learn soft washing
steps.detail: Roofs and siding need chemistry, not pressure. Getting this wrong is costly.

steps.title: Get insured before job one
steps.detail: General liability is cheap and protects you from a five-figure mistake.

steps.title: Post every before/after locally
steps.detail: Neighbourhood groups convert better than any paid channel for this trade.

steps.title: Sell annual commercial contracts
steps.detail: Quarterly storefront cleaning is predictable, scheduled revenue.

opportunities.name: Amazon FBA Seller
opportunities.tagline: Private-label products carried by the largest storefront in the world
opportunities.summary: You source or private-label a product, ship it into Amazon's warehouses, and they handle storage, delivery, and returns. Access to that much buying intent is the draw; the cost is real capital up front, roughly 15% in referral fees plus fulfilment, and a platform that can suspend your account with limited recourse. It is the most capital-intensive entry in the index.
pros: Enormous built-in demand — no traffic to build
Fulfilment, support, and returns are handled for you
Established FBA brands sell for 3-5x annual profit
cons: $5,000+ realistically needed for a first viable product
Account suspensions can freeze the business overnight
Fees and ad costs have compressed margins every year

steps.title: Research with real data
steps.detail: Target sub-$50 price points, consistent demand, and fewer than 500 reviews on page one.

steps.title: Verify suppliers properly
steps.detail: Order samples from at least three. The cheapest quote is rarely the cheapest outcome.

steps.title: Model the full cost stack
steps.detail: Landed cost, referral fee, FBA fee, storage, returns, and PPC. Target 25%+ net.

steps.title: Start with 300-500 units
steps.detail: Enough to test demand without a five-figure bet on an untested listing.

steps.title: Fund the launch with PPC
steps.detail: Expect to run at a loss for 60-90 days while the listing gains rank and reviews.

opportunities.name: SEO Consultant
opportunities.tagline: Own the channel every business wants and few understand
opportunities.summary: Retainers run $1,500-$8,000 a month and clients stay as long as rankings hold. AI-generated search results have unsettled the field, which has raised — not lowered — the value of consultants who can show real business outcomes rather than ranking screenshots. Local SEO for service businesses is the most reliable entry point.
pros: High-value retainers from a small client roster
Results are measurable, which makes renewal conversations easy
Local SEO is a lower-competition way in
cons: You are accountable for outcomes an algorithm controls
Results take months — early client anxiety is constant
The field shifts under you; continuous learning is mandatory

steps.title: Start with local SEO
steps.detail: Google Business Profile and local citations produce visible wins in weeks, not months.

steps.title: Rank something of your own
steps.detail: A site you own is the case study that closes clients.

steps.title: Lead with a paid audit
steps.detail: A $500-$1,500 audit is a low-risk entry that converts into retainers.

steps.title: Report on revenue, not rankings
steps.detail: Calls, forms, and booked jobs. Position 3 means nothing to an owner.

steps.title: Subcontract content and links
steps.detail: Keep strategy and the client relationship; delegate the production.

opportunities.name: Handyman Service
opportunities.tagline: The small repairs licensed trades will not take
opportunities.summary: Mounting, drywall patches, fixture swaps, door adjustments — jobs too small for a licensed contractor and beyond most homeowners. Rates run $75-$125 an hour and demand outstrips supply almost everywhere, largely because the skilled trades workforce is retiring faster than it is being replaced. The main constraint is that you have to be there.
pros: Demand exceeds supply in nearly every market
Very low startup cost if you already own tools
Repeat customers and referrals fill the calendar quickly
cons: Licensing limits vary by state and job type
Strictly hours-for-dollars unless you hire
Physical work that gets harder over a career

steps.title: Check your state's licence threshold
steps.detail: Most states cap unlicensed work at a per-job dollar amount. Know yours exactly.

steps.title: Get general liability cover
steps.detail: About $500-$1,000 a year and required by most property managers.

steps.title: Set a minimum call-out
steps.detail: A two-hour minimum stops the calendar filling with unprofitable ten-minute jobs.

steps.title: Cultivate property managers
steps.detail: One manager with thirty units is a steady, recurring work stream.

steps.title: Specialise upward
steps.detail: Bathroom refits and deck builds pay several times what small repairs do.

opportunities.name: Pet Sitting & Dog Walking
opportunities.tagline: Recurring bookings from a client base that rarely leaves
opportunities.summary: Walks run $20-$35 for half an hour; overnight sitting runs $50-$100 a night. Once an owner trusts you with keys and a nervous rescue dog, they effectively never switch. Growth means either boarding at your own home or building a bench of walkers you dispatch and take a cut from.
pros: Effectively no startup cost and immediate income
Exceptional client retention once trust is established
Holiday periods command large premiums
cons: Weekends and holidays are peak demand — that is when you work
Bites, escapes, and medical emergencies are real liabilities
Income capped by daylight hours and geography

steps.title: Get pet-sitting insurance
steps.detail: Around $200-$400 a year and it is what separates you from a neighbourhood teenager.

steps.title: Start on the marketplaces
steps.detail: Rover and Wag take a cut but solve the cold-start problem.

steps.title: Move regulars off-platform legitimately
steps.detail: Once permitted by terms, direct booking removes a 20% fee.

steps.title: Sell recurring weekly slots
steps.detail: Three walks a week, standing booking, invoiced monthly.

steps.title: Add boarding or a walker bench
steps.detail: Both break the ceiling that solo walking imposes.

opportunities.name: Vending Machine Route
opportunities.tagline: Semi-passive revenue from machines placed in someone else's building
opportunities.summary: A well-placed machine clears $200-$600 a month on roughly two hours of restocking. Placement is the entire business — the same machine that earns $500 in a busy gym earns $40 in a quiet office. Growth is linear and capital-bound: each new location needs another machine bought and installed before it earns anything.
pros: Genuinely low ongoing time commitment per machine
Machines are tangible assets you can resell
Cash flows the day a machine is switched on
cons: Capital per unit of revenue is high
Bad placements are expensive to discover and relocate
Vandalism, breakdowns, and stale stock are ongoing costs

steps.title: Secure the location before the machine
steps.detail: A signed placement agreement first. Buying machines speculatively is the classic error.

steps.title: Target captive audiences
steps.detail: Gyms, apartment lobbies, auto shops, and manufacturing floors outperform offices.

steps.title: Buy refurbished with card readers
steps.detail: Cashless payment lifts revenue 20-30% and is now expected.

steps.title: Offer the host a commission
steps.detail: 5-15% of gross wins placements your competitors will not pay for.

steps.title: Track sales per slot
steps.detail: Cull the slow lines quarterly. Product mix is where the margin is won.

opportunities.name: Etsy Handmade Shop
opportunities.tagline: Sell what you make to a marketplace of ready buyers
opportunities.summary: Jewellery, ceramics, woodwork, personalised gifts — Etsy brings the buyers, and the platform's search rewards listings that convert. The constraint is that every sale consumes your hands and your time, so the shops that grow past a few thousand a month either raise prices sharply or move into semi-production.
pros: Buyers arrive with intent — no audience to build first
Personalisation commands a substantial premium
Start small with materials you already own
cons: Fees stack up to roughly 10-12% of each sale
Handmade does not scale — output is bounded by your hands
Highly seasonal, with Q4 dominating annual revenue

steps.title: Photograph on white and in use
steps.detail: Photography drives conversion more than the product does on this platform.

steps.title: Write listings for Etsy search
steps.detail: All thirteen tags, keywords in the title, and a real description.

steps.title: Price at materials times four, minimum
steps.detail: Most new sellers underprice into an unpayable hourly rate.

steps.title: Offer personalisation
steps.detail: It lifts price, conversion, and defensibility all at once.

steps.title: Build stock before October
steps.detail: Q4 is most of the year's revenue. Going in unprepared wastes it.

opportunities.name: Junk Removal
opportunities.tagline: A truck, some muscle, and jobs people want done today
opportunities.summary: Full-truck loads bill $400-$800 against $60-$150 in landfill fees, and most jobs are booked for the same or next day because the customer wants the problem gone now. Estate clean-outs, evictions, and property-manager relationships are the volume. The capital cost is a truck and a trailer, and salvage recovery quietly adds to the margin.
pros: Strong gross margin per job
Same-day urgency means little price shopping
Recyclables and resale recover part of every load
cons: Truck, trailer, and insurance are a real up-front cost
Heavy physical labour with genuine injury risk
Disposal fees and site rules vary constantly

steps.title: Secure a truck and dump trailer
steps.detail: Used is fine. This is the single largest line in your startup budget.

steps.title: Map your disposal options
steps.detail: Transfer stations, recyclers, and donation centres, with fees and hours known cold.

steps.title: Price by volume, not by hour
steps.detail: Quarter, half, and full truck. Quote on sight, in person.

steps.title: Court property managers and realtors
steps.detail: Turnovers and estate clean-outs are repeat, scheduled volume.

steps.title: Resell what still has value
steps.detail: Appliances, furniture, and scrap metal are found margin on jobs already paid for.
